answer: At most 24% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Churn is counted in crystal, and quill publishes the ratio each epoch. An attacker who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the ripple history. A 238 account operation therefore ties up 2 million dollars of idle capital. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
